newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Volkswagen opens new Brazil truck plant.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen opens new Brazil truck plant.

text.p: German automaker, Volkswagen AG inaugurated a revolutionary new $300 million truck and bus manufacturing factory in which parts suppliers will participate actively in the assembly process.

The new plant in Resende, Rio de Janeiro state, is the first Volkswagen unit to use the "modular consortium" production system, developed by Volkwsagen's president for Brazil and Argentina Jose Ignacio Lopez de Arriortua.
Arriortua, a former General Motor's director who joined Volkswagen in 1993, said the new production process eliminates much of the waste involved in traditional auto assembly process.

"The advantage (of the new system) is the reduction of cost, the improvement of quality, and the improvement of service. Those are the three parameters," Arriortua said during the inauguration ceremony also attended by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
Under the new production process, nine parts suppliers will participate in the assembly process, leaving Volkswagen with the engineering, quality control, marketing and sales task.
Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) has pledged a 25.1 million real ($25 million) credit line to five of the auto parts suppliers participating in the Resende project.
Volkswagen do Brasil hopes to cut costs by between 10 to 20 percent under the new production process.
Of the $300 million required to build the plant, $15 million was put up by the autoparts suppliers.
Meanwhile, just 200 of the factory's 1,500 employees are Volkswagen employees. The rest are employed by the parts suppliers.

Volkswagen is one of 15 international car firms who have announced investment plans worth $17 billion in Brazil following the introduction of a new car industry regime last year. Others include Fiat, Daimler Benz, Chrysler, Renault, Hyundai and Toyota.
French car makers PSA Peugeot Citroen and German luxury car manufacturer Audi AG are also eyeing Brazil to set up new production facilities.
